headline_en: Moving strategically to rescue sailors held hostage by pirates: Foreign Minister
summary_en: On 19 March 2024 Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the government was pursuing various strategies to free 23 Bangladeshi sailors held hostage by Somali pirates, along with their ship. After meeting the UAE ambassador he said talks with the UAE covered making transfer of "akama" (work permission) from one employer to another easier and issuing work permits to Bangladeshis in emirates other than Dubai. The rest of the article is domestic politics.

facts.statement: As of 19 March 2024, 23 Bangladeshi sailors were held hostage by pirates in Somalia together with a Bangladeshi ship; Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the government was using various strategies to free the sailors safely and also free the ship.

Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said on 19 March 2024 that not everything about the hostage sailors could be disclosed, asked media to report carefully, and declined to comment on a Reuters report about the hijacked Bangladeshi ship.

Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said on 19 March 2024 that during his recent bilateral visit to the UAE and in a meeting with UAE ambassador Abdulla Ali Abdulla Khasif Almudi in Dhaka, Bangladesh discussed making it easier to transfer an "akama" (permission to work) from one employer to another in the UAE.

Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said on 19 March 2024 that Bangladesh discussed with the UAE (including with its foreign and employment minister during a recent visit) the issuing of work permits to Bangladeshis in regions of the UAE other than Dubai.

headline_en: Facebook romance: woman in trouble after giving over 1 crore taka
summary_en: A man from Narail, Benojir Hossain (40), posing on Facebook as "Shahid Hasan", a US-based Bangladeshi-born pilot, promised to marry a divorced bank officer and take her to the USA, and took 1 crore 9 lakh taka from her for passport, visa and other pretexts. CTTC arrested him after she filed a case at Wari police station in November 2023; she later settled with him for 60 lakh taka because of debt pressure, and he got bail.

facts.statement: Benojir Hossain (40) of Narail, Bangladesh, sent a Facebook friend request under the name "Shahid Hasan", claimed to be a pilot and Bangladeshi-born US citizen living in New York, gathered the woman's personal details over Messenger, told an emotional story of being an orphan, proposed marriage and promised to take her to the USA.

The fraudster asked for money repeatedly for passport, visa and other pretexts to take the woman to America; she sold 37 bhori of gold jewellery, cashed savings certificates, took a bank loan, borrowed from relatives and sent money to 13 mobile financial service numbers he gave.
A divorced woman bank officer paid 1 crore 9 lakh taka to the fraudster who promised to marry her and take her to the USA, according to the CTTC report submitted to court.
When the woman went to the Khulna address he had given and found no "Shahid Hasan" there, the fraudster threatened to leak private videos on social media.

The woman filed a case at Wari police station, Dhaka, in November 2023; the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit arrested Benojir in Narail soon after; investigating officer SI Md. Sumon of the CTTC Cyber Terrorism Investigation division said the taking of the money was verified.

In a compromise petition filed in court on 28 January 2024, the victim said she had received money from the accused and did not object to his bail; she told Prothom Alo she settled for 60 lakh taka because she could not repay bank and personal debts; the court then granted bail.
facts.source_in_article: victim; defence lawyer Sheikh Enamul Hasan

headline_en: Strongest passport index: which country is top, where is Bangladesh
summary_en: In the 2024 Henley & Partners passport index Bangladesh rose one place to 97th, with visa-free access to 42 countries (40 the previous year). In Canadian firm Arton Capital's 2024 index Bangladesh rose two places to 90th, with 19 visa-free countries, 31 visa-on-arrival and 148 requiring a visa.

facts.statement: In the 2024 Henley & Partners passport index, Bangladesh ranked 97th (up from 98th the previous year), sharing the rank with North Korea; Bangladeshi passport holders could travel to 42 countries without a prior visa, up from 40 the previous year.

In the 2024 Henley & Partners index, Sri Lanka ranked 96th; Nepal, Libya and Palestine 98th; India 80th with 62 countries without prior visa; Afghanistan last (104th) with 28; top six (France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Singapore, Spain) had 194 countries.

In Canadian firm Arton Capital's 2024 passport index, Bangladesh rose two places to 90th; Bangladeshi passport holders could go to 19 countries without a prior visa, needed a visa on arrival in 31 countries and needed a visa for 148 countries.
In Arton Capital's 2024 index the UAE passport was the strongest; India was 68th, Nepal 86th, Pakistan 92nd, Yemen 91st and Syria last at 96th.

headline_en: Foreign worker fraud: 20 detained in Malaysia including 11 Bangladeshis
summary_en: On 8 October 2026 Malaysia's Immigration Department (JIM) raided premises in Taman Datuk Ahmad Razali and detained 20 people, including 11 Bangladeshis, over foreign worker quota fraud. The syndicate allegedly used an "A-to-B" method: company A got approval and brought workers on PLKS temporary employment passes, then supplied them for profit to company B. 265 Bangladeshi passports were seized; profit per worker was estimated at RM 3,800 to 5,000.

facts.statement: On Thursday 8 October 2026, from 7:30 am, Malaysia's Immigration Department (JIM) intelligence and special operations division from Putrajaya headquarters, with two divisions of the Inland Revenue Board (IRB), raided premises in Taman Datuk Ahmad Razali and detained 20 people aged 23 to 47, including 11 Bangladeshis, for alleged involvement in foreign-worker quota fraud.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: Those detained in the 8 October 2026 Malaysian raid were two Bangladeshi men believed to be owner and manager of the business, 6 local women staff, and 12 foreign customers: 9 Bangladeshi men and 3 Indonesian women.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: In the raid the team seized 265 Bangladeshi, 63 Indonesian, 12 Pakistani and 1 Indian passports, and RM 6,700 believed to be money paid by customers.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: The syndicate used an "A-to-B" method: a company (employer A) got approval to bring foreign workers and brought them under the PLKS temporary employment pass, but the workers were then supplied for profit to another company (employer B) instead of working for the original employer; the syndicate is also suspected of submitting false company information to obtain foreign-worker quota approvals.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: Further investigation found that foreign workers brought into Malaysia did not work for the companies that applied for the quota, but worked independently at other companies.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: The syndicate is believed to have made a profit of RM 3,800 to RM 5,000 for each worker brought to Malaysia; the companies understated profits to evade tax and did not file personal income returns from 2020 to 2023.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

facts.statement: Malaysia's Immigration Department said it will keep taking strict action against all illegal activity, including those who plan, run and profit from misuse of foreign-worker quotas; the raid was based on public tip-offs and the department's own intelligence.
facts.source_in_article: JIM Director General Datuk Zakaria Shaaban

summary_en: The Asia-Pacific Institute for Broadcasting Development (AIBD), an intergovernmental body linked to Bangladesh Betar, is recruiting a Programme Coordinator in Kuala Lumpur open to Bangladeshi citizens. Requirements, one-year contract terms, application email and the 27 March 2026 deadline are given.

facts.statement: The Asia-Pacific Institute for Broadcasting Development (AIBD), an intergovernmental organisation connected with Bangladesh Betar, is recruiting a Programme Coordinator (Programme department) to work in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Bangladeshi citizens can apply.

AIBD Programme Coordinator requirements: at least a bachelor's degree in mass communication, computer science, IT, telecommunications, social science, public relations, event management or related subject; 3 to 5 years' experience in development or project management; written and spoken English; experience organising training and consultancy; age under 40. Preferred: professional training in TV or radio production, content or documentary, and skills in social media management, publication design and presentations.
The AIBD post is first a one-year contract, which may be extended depending on performance and organisational need; salary and allowances are per the organisation's policy.

To apply for the AIBD post, email the application with CV and copies of educational and professional certificates, a passport-size photo taken within the last six months, information on dependent family members who may live in Kuala Lumpur if appointed, and recommendation letters if needed; deadline 27 March 2026.
AIBD application email: admin@aibd.org.my

headline_en: Six years in Canada: US will not return Bangladeshi detained at border
summary_en: Mahin Shahriar, a Bangladeshi-origin refugee claimant living in Canada since 2019, accidentally crossed into the US on 12 May 2025 while following a friend's directions near Montreal and is held by ICE in Buffalo. ICE is ready to return him to Canada but the Canada Border Services Agency has not approved his entry; his lawyer Wasim Ahmed has sought an urgent Federal Court hearing. His first asylum claim had been rejected because it was filed through a fraudulent immigration consultant.

facts.statement: On 12 May 2025 Mahin Shahriar, a Bangladeshi-origin refugee claimant in Canada, followed a friend's phone directions to an address near Montreal very close to the border, unknowingly crossed into the US, reported to border guards, and was detained; as of October 2025 he was in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody in Buffalo.
ICE was ready to send Mahin Shahriar back to Canada, but the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) did not approve his entry; ICE cannot deport him to Bangladesh because he has no travel document.
CBSA said by email that it does not comment on individuals detained abroad and that each entry decision is made case by case.

Under the Safe Third Country Agreement, there is a rule that an asylum claimant linked to Canada detained in the US is to be returned to Canada within 14 days; Shahriar's lawyer believes he should be taken back under it.
US immigration authorities acknowledged that Mahin Shahriar could face torture if sent back to Bangladesh.
Mahin Shahriar's first asylum application in Canada was rejected because it was filed through a fraudulent immigration consultant; his lawyer says this and the stress led to his breakdown.

Lawyer Wasim Ahmed applied for an urgent hearing at the Federal Court to compel Canada to take Shahriar back on humanitarian grounds, noting he has lived in Canada since 2019, his mother has refugee status and his sister is a full-time student there.

headline_en: Bangladeshi youth burned in Iraq dies; uncertainty over getting body back due to Middle East conflict
summary_en: Mohammad Ali (25) of Bhola Sadar, who went to Iraq in 2020 and worked at a company in Baghdad, was burned in a generator room fire at work on 15 June 2025 and died in hospital on Wednesday 18 June. The employer has no objection to sending the body home or burying it in Iraq, but flights from Iraq were suspended because of the Iran-Israel conflict and legal processes will take time. Bhola's DC said no ministry letter had arrived yet.

facts.statement: On 15 June 2025 Mohammad Ali (25), son of Saleh Ahmed of East Bapta Cheuakhali village, Bapta union, Bhola Sadar upazila, was seriously burned in a fire/generator explosion in the generator room of his workplace in Baghdad, Iraq; he died in a Baghdad hospital on Wednesday 18 June 2025 and his family learned on Thursday 19 June.
The employer told Ali's family it had no objection to sending the body to Bangladesh, and the family could also choose burial in Iraq.
Because of the Iran-Israel conflict, flights from Iraq were suspended for the time being in June 2025, making repatriation of Ali's body uncertain; completing legal procedures would also take time.
Bhola Deputy Commissioner Azad Jahan said no letter on the case had come from the ministry yet, perhaps would after offices reopen, and then the administration would contact the family and act.
Ali went to Iraq in 2020; he last visited home in November 2024 and had borrowed money from the company owner to build a house in Bangladesh; his income supported a 9-member family.

headline_en: 15 Bangladeshis detained trying to enter Malaysia posing as cricketers
summary_en: Malaysia's Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) detained 15 Bangladeshis at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday 17 March 2025 who wore cricket uniforms and showed a letter from a tournament organiser that turned out to be fake. No tournament was found for 21 to 23 March, and the named "sponsor" knew nothing of it; AKPS believes they are part of a syndicate and will act under immigration law.

facts.statement: On Monday 17 March 2025 Malaysia's Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) detained 15 Bangladeshis at Kuala Lumpur International Airport accused of trying to enter the country posing as cricket players.

The 15 Bangladeshis wore cricket uniforms and showed a letter from a tournament organiser saying a cricket tournament would be held 21 to 23 March; investigation found the letter fake, no cricket event at that time, and the person shown as "sponsor" said he knew nothing about the tournament.
AKPS found no evidence the 15 were cricket players, believes they were part of a syndicate entering Malaysia for another purpose, and said action would be taken against them under immigration law.

headline_en: Bangladeshi kidnapped in Saudi Arabia, 35 lakh taka ransom collected; three arrested in Bangladesh
summary_en: A gang of expatriate Bangladeshis kidnapped long-time Saudi resident Russell in Riyadh on 11 January 2025, tortured him and collected 35 lakh taka ransom from his family through a bank account they supplied. After his father-in-law filed a case at Khilgaon police station on 21 January, police arrested three people in Lakshmipur and Brahmanbaria on 31 January; 12 lakh taka has been frozen by court order. The article also has an unrelated item on teen gang arrests.

facts.statement: On 11 January 2025 members of an organised kidnapping gang of expatriate Bangladeshis abducted Russell (রাসেল), a Bangladeshi long resident in Saudi Arabia, from Riyadh, tortured him, and demanded 35 lakh taka ransom from his family in Bangladesh.
Russell's family deposited 35 lakh taka ransom into a bank account given by the kidnapping gang.

After Russell's father-in-law Kamrul Islam filed a case at Khilgaon police station, Dhaka, on 21 January 2025, Khilgaon police arrested Akram (33), Md. Ismail Hossain (34) and Mojib Rahman (26) in raids in Lakshmipur and Brahmanbaria on Friday 31 January 2025; 12 lakh taka of the 35 lakh ransom was frozen by court order.

headline_en: Bangladeshi dies of mpox in UAE; buried in Cumilla following health rules
summary_en: Kamal Hossain (38) of Meshtala village, Chauddagram, Cumilla, who had worked at a company in the UAE for about seven years, died of mpox in a Sharjah hospital. His body arrived at Dhaka airport on the night of 10 October 2024 and was buried under health ministry and district administration instructions on 11 October, with officials present; eight family members are under observation. The article gives two different death dates (3 September and 30 September).

facts.statement: Kamal Hossain (38), son of Nazir Ahmed of Meshtala village, Munshirhat union, Chauddagram upazila, Cumilla, who had gone to the UAE about 7 years earlier and worked at a company, died of mpox (monkeypox) at a hospital in Sharjah; the article says once he died on 3 September and elsewhere on 30 September.
Kamal Hossain's body reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, on Thursday night 10 October 2024, was driven home under administration security and arrived at 7:20 am on 11 October.

The body of the mpox victim was buried at 8 am on Friday 11 October 2024 after janaza, following Health Ministry and district administration instructions with maximum caution; upazila officials, law enforcement and health officials were present to make sure health rules were followed.
facts.source_in_article: Chauddagram UNO Mohammad Rahmat Ullah; OC ATM Akhtar Uz Zaman

facts.statement: Eight members of Kamal Hossain's family were placed under observation; the upazila health officer said no mpox patient had been found in Bangladesh so far to his knowledge.

headline_en: Dubai-based Bangladeshi wins 65 crore taka in lottery
summary_en: Bangladeshi expatriate Abul Monsur Abdus Sabur (50) in Dubai won 2 crore (20 million) dirhams, over 65 crore taka, in the Big Ticket lottery announced on 3 October 2024; he had played since 2007 and bought five tickets with friends. The article also describes Big Ticket's next draws and prizes.

facts.statement: Bangladeshi expatriate Abul Monsur Abdus Sabur (50) won 2 crore dirhams (over 65 crore taka) in the Big Ticket lottery in the UAE, with winners announced on Thursday 3 October 2024; he had taken part since 2007 and recently bought five tickets with some friends.

Big Ticket began selling new tickets on 2 October 2024, with a daily gold bar prize, a grand draw on 3 November with a top prize of 2 crore dirhams, a Range Rover worth 3.5 lakh dirhams and a BMW worth 4.7 lakh dirhams.

headline_en: Bangladeshi youth killed by car in Saudi Arabia
summary_en: Mister Ali (38) of Adarvita village, Madarganj, Jamalpur, who went to Saudi Arabia two and a half years earlier and worked as a street cleaner, was hit and killed by an out-of-control private car while working on a road on the morning of Sunday 28 July 2024. His family, who depended on his income, asked for the body to be returned at government expense.

facts.statement: On the morning of Sunday 28 July 2024, Mister Ali (38), son of Nazrul Islam of Adarvita village, Adarvita union, Madarganj upazila, Jamalpur, working as a street cleaner on a city road in Saudi Arabia, was run over from behind by an out-of-control private car and died on the spot; Saudi law enforcement recovered the body.
Mister Ali's younger brother Razzak Ali asked that the body be delivered to the village home as soon as possible at government expense.
Mister Ali went to Saudi Arabia two and a half years before July 2024 and worked as a road cleaner; he was the family's sole earner, leaving a wife and two small children.
